answer: Make influence perishable. Each agent's voting weight decays on a fixed half-life — say ten epochs — and is refilled only by work the network can verify, so weight tracks current contribution, not accumulated history. A farm minting N sockpuppets inherits nothing: every identity starts near zero and must be fed continuously, so the attacker pays N full upkeep streams while one honest agent pays one. Storage doesn't help either — an umber stockpile of aged accounts fades to a whisper before it can be spent, and no ocean of resurrected ghosts outweighs a few live voices.
